results.title: GES to reprimand two Techiman SHS teachers who allegedly assaulted student in viral video
results.content: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has announced disciplinary measures against teachers of the Twene Amanfo Senior High Technical School in Techiman who allegedly assaulted students, following an incident captured in a viral video.

results.title: Trust and collaboration are key to preventing violent extremism – NPC Chairman
results.content: The Chairman of the National Peace Council, Most Rev. Emmanuel Kofi Fianu, has called for a united national effort involving security agencies, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, families and local communities to prevent violent extremism.

results.title: Ghana must not confuse access to AI tools with readiness for AI-powered education – KNUST AI coordinator
results.content: The Coordinator of AI Courses at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Prof. Eric Appau Asante, has called for practical national and institutional guidelines to regulate the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, warning that access to the technology alone does not guarantee its effective integration into teaching and learning.

results.title: Five transport unions threaten nationwide shutdown over trading activities at bus stops
results.content: Commercial transport services across Ghana could be affected on Wednesday, November 4, after five transport unions announced plans to withdraw services to protest trading at bus stops and on pedestrian walkways.

results.title: Motorists caught speeding above 130km/h where 50km/h is permitted as Traffitech begins operation
results.content: The Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) has recorded thousands of speeding offences on the first day of the implementation of its Traffitech system, with some motorists caught travelling above 130km/h on roads with a 50km/h speed limit.

results.content: The Ghana Police Service says the introduction of its automated traffic enforcement system, TraffiTech-GH, is expected to significantly reduce road crashes, injuries and fatalities.

results.content: Litigants seeking legal redress have been left stranded at court premises in Kumasi as critical staff of the judiciary lay down their tools over its 2026 salary review and outstanding arrears.

results.title: JUSAG strike begins to bite as courts shut down in Accra
results.content: The nationwide industrial action declared by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) has affected court operations across the country, forcing the closure of several court premises, including the Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, Accra Circuit Court and some District Courts.

results.title: Muntaka calls for stronger law enforcement cooperation to tackle transnational crimes
results.content: The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, has called for stronger cooperation and information sharing among law enforcement agencies to tackle the growing threat of transnational crimes and strengthen national and regional security.

results.title: GoldBod generates $1.011bn in forex from gold trade in October
results.content: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) says it generated US$1.011 billion in foreign exchange from its artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold trading operations in October 2026.

results.title: GES cancels two-day mid-term break for basic schools in November
results.content: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has cancelled the two-day mid-term break scheduled for basic schools on November 5 and 6, 2026, as part of efforts to make up for instructional time lost during the recent industrial action.

results.title: GMet warns of possible drop in Volta River inflows amid El Niño conditions
results.content: The Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) has warned that persistent El Niño conditions could reduce water inflows into the Volta River system, with potential implications for hydroelectric power generation at the Akosombo Dam.

results.title: El Niño conditions threaten prolonged dry spells, food production in Ghana – GMet
results.content: The Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) has warned that persistent El Niño conditions could expose parts of Ghana to prolonged dry spells, potentially affecting agricultural production and food security.

results.title: Encroachment along Pokuase-Nsawam Highway raises road safety concerns at Dobro
results.content: Concerns over road safety and the progress of construction works along the Pokuase–Nsawam Highway have resurfaced following the emergence of container shops, sand and chippings businesses, and concrete mixer rental services within a road buffer zone at Dobro in the Eastern Region.

results.title: Kofi Arko Nokoe commissions Apataim cassava factory to boost local processing
results.content: The Apataim Cassava Factory Project in the Evalue Ajomoro Gwira Constituency has been commissioned, marking a step towards expanding local cassava processing, creating jobs and improving incomes for farmers and processors.

results.title: GHS contains yellow fever outbreak after confirming four cases
results.content: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) says it has contained a yellow fever outbreak recorded between September and the first half of October, after laboratory tests confirmed four cases in parts of the country.

results.title: Ghana will become hostile territory for drug traffickers – Kumadoe
results.content: Security analyst Richard Kumadoe says Ghana is stepping up efforts to disrupt international drug trafficking networks, warning that traffickers who use the country as a transit point risk arrest either locally or at their intended destinations.

results.title: GRASAG-UG, UGSRC warn students against unauthorised protest over accommodation fees
results.content: The Graduate Students’ Association of Ghana (GRASAG-UG) and the University of Ghana Students’ Representative Council (UGSRC) have urged students to stay away from a planned demonstration over accommodation fees, warning that the group organising the protest is not recognised under the university’s governance system.

results.title: Bagbin urges voters to scrutinise campaign promises, resist political propaganda
results.content: The Speaker of Parliament, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, has called on Ghanaians, particularly young people, to take a more critical approach to political campaigns by questioning promises and examining policy proposals before making electoral choices.
